articles.title: Policy rate raised to 2 per cent
articles.expand: Stronger economic activity combined with cost increases due to supply disruptions mean that inflation is expected to continue rising going forward. The Executive Board has therefore decided to raise the policy rate by 0.25 percentage points to 2 per cent. If the outlook for inflation and economic activity holds, it is likely that the policy rate will be raised further in the coming year, in line with the policy rate forecast in September.

articles.title: The Riksbank plans to finance part of the foreign currency reserve with foreign currency loans via the Swedish National Debt Office
articles.expand: To reduce currency risk on its balance sheet, the Riksbank plans to finance the equivalent of around SEK 200 billion of the foreign currency reserve with foreign currency loans via the Swedish National Debt Office. The intention is also to replace the FX swaps that the Riksbank has used for currency hedging since 2023. This change is not intended to affect the long-term size of the foreign currency reserve and does not serve any monetary policy purpose.
